title: Qlik Engine Memory and RAM Pressure

dataSources: Qlik Sense logs (`qlik:scheduler`, `qlik:engine`, `qlik:proxy`), reload task history, section access audit, Qlik Cloud events (`com.qlik.v1.*`) and app/reload metrics via REST. Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Qlik Sense Enterprise logs (Scheduler/Engine/Proxy/Repository) via Universal Forwarder; Qlik Cloud events via the Qlik Cloud REST API through HEC scripted inputs. — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=bi sourcetype=qlik:engine metric=ram_committed_bytes
| bin _time span=5m
| stats max(value) as ram_bytes by host, _time
| eval ram_gb=round(ram_bytes/1024/1024/1024,1)
| where ram_gb>200
| sort - _time
description: Alerts on UC-24.4.2 — Qlik, Engine, Memory, and, RAM — using `index=bi` sourcetype `qlik:engine`, grouped by `host`, `_time`. Outputs `ram_bytes` each `5m`; alert when `ram_gb` > 200. Primary focus: RAM Pressure. Purpose-built for 'Qlik Engine Memory and RAM Pressure' in Operations workflows.
value: UC-24.4.2 operationalises 'Qlik Engine Memory and RAM Pressure' against `qlik:engine` feeds so operators reduce operational risk and delayed incident response without manual correlation.
implementation: Ingest engine metrics; schedule every 5 minutes; tune the threshold to node RAM; alert before exhaustion. Rebalance apps across nodes.
visualization: Timechart of engine RAM per node, alert on high usage.

2. **Batch `max` on `qlik:engine`** — Scheduled automation elevates `_time` without crossing `ram_gb` > 200 for UC-24.4.2. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `host`, `_time`** — Health checks in `bi` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `qlik:engine`** — First 48h baseline for UC-24.4.2 on `host` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `host`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Qlik Sense Enterprise logs (Scheduler/Engine/Proxy/Repository) via Universal Forwarder; Qlik Cloud events via the Qlik Cloud REST API through HEC scripted inputs. — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=qlik:engine into bi. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`_time, host, ram_gb`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
